articles.title: Amroha Wedding Turns Into Chaos as Girlfriend Storms Ceremony, Accuses Groom of 8-Year Relationship
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dramatic scene unfolded in Uttar Pradesh’s Amroha district when a woman barged into a nikah ceremony and accused the groom of being in a relationship with her for the past eight years. The incident took place in Dhakkha village under the Said Nagli police station area.

body.html:
A dramatic scene unfolded in Uttar Pradesh’s Amroha district when a woman barged into a nikah ceremony and accused the groom of being in a relationship with her for the past eight years. The incident took place in Dhakkha village under the Said Nagli police station area.

According to police, during the marriage ceremony, a young woman named Anam suddenly arrived and created a ruckus, claiming that the groom, Afsaar, had promised to marry her and had “ruined her future” for eight years. She shouted that the nikah could not proceed unless he married her instead.

The groom, however, denied knowing her. This triggered further drama, as the woman presented proof and claimed she was the daughter of his maternal uncle, questioning how he could refuse to recognize her.

Following the confrontation, the wedding came to an abrupt halt. The groom’s family, unable to pacify the woman or clarify the situation, ultimately returned without performing the nikah. The bride’s side also expressed anger toward the groom.

Police arrived at the spot, took both parties to the police station to maintain peace and order, and halted the marriage. During the preliminary investigation, it was revealed that an FIR related to the matter had already been registered by the woman at Tonk City Police Station in Ghaziabad, where she has accused the groom of rape.

Amroha Police said communication has been established with the investigating officer in Ghaziabad, and all necessary information has been forwarded. They added that appropriate legal action is being taken based on the complaint.

articles.title: Prayagraj Shock: Soldier Murders Minor Girlfriend, Buries Body in Orchard to Hide Upcoming Wedding
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 26-year-old soldier from Prayagraj has been arrested for murdering his minor girlfriend after she insisted that he marry her.

body.html:
A 26-year-old soldier from Prayagraj has been arrested for murdering his minor girlfriend after she insisted that he marry her. Police said the accused, identified as Harshvardhan Singh alias Deepak, strangled and stabbed the girl before burying her body in an orchard in Lakhranwa village.

The victim, an intermediate student, had known the accused since June 2025 through Instagram. Harshvardhan, a Naik posted in Patiala, is a resident of Kusumgur village in Tharwai. His marriage was scheduled for 30 November, which the girl opposed. She reportedly threatened to approach the police, angering the soldier, who decided to “remove her from his way”.

According to police, on 10 November, Harshvardhan called the girl to meet him. He picked her up near Balan intersection and spent the day with her near Company Garden. By evening, he took her to an orchard, where he first strangled her with her scarf. After she fell unconscious, he stabbed her with a knife he had bought a day earlier, and then buried her body.

A breakthrough came the next day when the girl’s bag was recovered. A book inside contained the soldier’s name and mobile number, helping investigators link him to the crime. A vermilion box was also found in the bag.

Police arrested Harshvardhan from his home. He admitted that he had planned the murder on 9 November, buying the knife beforehand. After the crime, he repeatedly deleted chats and browser history from the girl’s Instagram and email accounts to destroy evidence.

On 15 November, the forensic team and dog squad inspected the orchard where the body was found—located just 1.5 km from the soldier’s house, a place he knew well.

Harshvardhan joined the Army in 2018. His name had earlier surfaced in a theft incident at a wedding, though no case was registered at the time.

DCP Ganganagar Kuldeep Singh Gunawat said the accused tried to delete digital evidence after the murder. DCP City Manish Kumar Shandilya confirmed that the book in the girl’s bag played a crucial role in cracking the case.
